newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan rivals claim northern town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan rivals claim northern town.

text.p: Afghan opposition forces said on Saturday they had retaken the northern town of Kunduz from the Taleban Islamic militia.
But the claim was denied by Taleban government Interior Minister Khairullah Khairkhwa in the capital Kabul.
A spokesman for ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani told reporters by telephone that forces loyal to the ousted government had taken control of the town after a deal with local commanders.
"The flag of the (ousted) government is fluttering in Kunduz," Rabbani's spokesman, Dr Abdullah, said.

But Khairkhwa told reporters: "Kunduz city and its districts are as a whole with the Taleban and their supporters. The situation is calm today after our forces killed 500 (ethnic) Uzbek armed men on Thursday in the fighting.
On Tuesday, Pro-Taleban forces had captured Kunduz, about 250 km (160 miles) north of Kabul, forcing a commander loyal to Rabbani to flee.
